nodes.summary: Let $s_1, s_2, p_1, p_2, q_1, q_2$ be natural numbers with $p_1, p_2 > 0$, $\gcd(p_1, q_1) = 1$, $\gcd(p_2, q_2) = 1$ and $\gcd(q_1, q_2) > 1$, and let $x = s_1 + p_1/q_1$ and $d = s_2 + p_2/q_2$. For indices $i, i', j, j' \in \{1, \dots, q_2 - 1\}$: if $x + id$ and $x + i'd$ are both nonnegative integers then $i = i'$; if $2x + jd$ and $2x + j'd$ are both nonnegative integers then $j = j'$; and if $x + id$ and…
nodes.title: Uniqueness of integer points when the denominators share a factor

nodes.summary: Let $s_1, s_2, p_1, p_2, q_1, q_2$ be natural numbers with $\gcd(p_1, q_1) = 1$, $\gcd(q_1, q_2) = 1$ and $q_1 \ge 3$, and let $x = s_1 + p_1/q_1$ and $d = s_2 + p_2/q_2$. Then for all natural numbers $i$ and $j$, neither $x + id$ nor $2x + jd$ is a nonnegative integer.
nodes.title: No integer points for coprime denominators, the first at least 3

nodes.summary: Let $s_1, s_2, p_2, q_2$ be natural numbers with $q_2$ odd, and let $x = s_1 + 1/2$ and $d = s_2 + p_2/q_2$. Then $x + id$ is not a nonnegative integer for any natural number $i$.
nodes.title: No integer points for a half-integer start and an odd denominator

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be an irrational real number and $d$ a rational number. Then for all natural numbers $i$ and $j$, neither $x + id$ nor $2x + jd$ is a nonnegative integer.
nodes.title: No nonnegative integer points for an irrational start and a rational difference

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a rational number that is not a nonnegative integer, and let $d$ be an irrational real number. Then $x + id$ is not a nonnegative integer for any natural number $i$, and $2x + jd$ is not a nonnegative integer for any natural number $j \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Nonnegative integer points for a rational start and an irrational difference

nodes.summary: For a real number $x$, a natural number $m$ and a real number $d \ne 0$, the progression $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$ has exactly $m + 1$ elements.
nodes.title: Size of the progression $J(x, m, d)$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the set $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ of real numbers has exactly $n$ elements.
nodes.title: Size of the interval $I_n$

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $d$ be real numbers with $d$ irrational. If $i$ and $j$ are natural numbers such that $x + id$ and $x + jd$ are both nonnegative integers, then $i = j$.
nodes.title: At most one nonnegative integer point on a progression with irrational difference

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a real number, let $s, p, q$ be natural numbers with $0 < p < q$ and $\gcd(p, q) = 1$, and let $d = s + p/q$. If $i, j \in \{1, \dots, q - 1\}$ and $x + id$ and $x + jd$ are both nonnegative integers, then $i = j$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of a nonnegative integer point for a rational difference

nodes.summary: A finite set $A$ of real numbers is an *MSTD set* (more sums than differences) when its difference set has fewer elements than its sumset: $|A - A| < |A + A|$, where $A + A = \{a + b : a, b \in A\}$ and $A - A = \{a - b : a, b \in A\}$.
nodes.title: MSTD set

nodes.summary: Let $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$, as finite sets of reals. For natural numbers $n \ge 3$, $m \ge 2$ and $x \ge n + 1$, and a positive irrational real number $d$, the set $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: Interval plus irrational-step progression with natural start is not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$, as finite sets of reals. Let $n \ge 3$ and $m$ be natural numbers, $d$ a positive irrational real number and $x > n - 1$ a real number that is not a natural number, and suppose that $x + jd$ is a natural number for some integer $j$ with $1 \le j \le m$. Then $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: Interval plus irrational-step progression meeting the naturals is not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$, as finite sets of reals. Let $n \ge 3$ and $m$ be natural numbers, $d$ a positive irrational real number and $x > n - 1$ a real number such that none of $x + id$ for $i = 0, 1, \dots, m$ is a natural number. Then $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: Interval plus irrational-step progression avoiding the naturals is not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$, as finite sets of reals. For natural numbers $n \ge 3$, $m \ge 2$, $d \ge 2$ and $x \le n - 1$, the set $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: Interval plus integer progression starting inside the interval is not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$, as finite sets of reals. For natural numbers $n \ge 3$, $m \ge 2$, $d \ge 2$ and $x$ with $n + 1 \le x \le 2n - 2$, the set $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: Interval plus integer progression starting in $(n + 1, 2n - 2)$ is not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$, as finite sets of reals. For natural numbers $n \ge 3$, $m \ge 2$, $d \ge 2$ and $x > n - 1$, the set $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: Interval plus integer progression starting after the interval is not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$, as finite sets of reals. For natural numbers $n \ge 3$, $m \ge 2$, $d \ge 2$ and $x \ge 2n - 1$, the set $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: Interval plus integer progression starting at $2n - 1$ or later is not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$, as finite sets of reals. Let $n \ge 3$, $m \ge 2$, $s_1$, $s_2$ and $p_2$ be natural numbers and $q_2$ an odd natural number, and let $x = s_1 + 1/2$ and $d = s_2 + p_2/q_2$. If $x < n - 1 < d$, then $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: Interval plus progression with half-integer start and odd-denominator step is not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$, as finite sets of reals. Let $n \ge 3$, $m \ge 2$, $s$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $2 \le d \le n - 1$, and let $x = s + 1/2$. If $x < n - 1$, then $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: Interval plus integer-step progression with half-integer start is not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$, $m \ge 2$ and $d \ge n$ be natural numbers, and let $x$ be a real number with $0 < x < n - 1$ that is not a natural number. Write $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$. Then $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: Interval plus progression with non-integer start and integer step at least $n$ is not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and $m \ge 2$ be natural numbers, and let $x$ and $d$ be real numbers with $0 < x < n - 1$. Write $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$. Suppose that one of the following holds: (i) $x$ is irrational, and $d$ is rational but not a positive integer; (ii) $x$ is rational but not a natural number, and $d$ is irrational; (iii) there are natural numbers…
nodes.title: An interval and an overlapping progression with incompatible start and step are not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$, $m \ge 2$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $2 \le d \le n - 1$, and let $x$ be a real number with $0 < x < n - 1$ such that either $x$ is irrational or $x = s + p/q$ for natural numbers $s, p, q$ with $0 < p < q$, $q \ne 2$ and $\gcd(p, q) = 1$. Write $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$. Then $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: An interval and an overlapping progression with small integer step are not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and $m \ge 2$ be natural numbers, and let $s_1, s_2, p_1, p_2, q_1, q_2$ be natural numbers with $p_1 > 0$, $p_2 > 0$, $\gcd(p_1, q_1) = \gcd(p_2, q_2) = 1$ and $\gcd(q_1, q_2) > 1$. Let $x = s_1 + p_1/q_1$ and $d = s_2 + p_2/q_2$, where a fraction with denominator $0$ is read as $0$, and suppose that $x < n - 1 < d$. Write $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and…
nodes.title: An interval and an overlapping progression whose denominators share a factor are not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$, $m$ and $x$ be natural numbers with $x \ge n + 1$, and let $d = s + p/q$, where $s, p, q$ are natural numbers with $0 < p < q$ and $\gcd(p, q) = 1$. Suppose that $m \ge q$ and $qd \le n - 1$. Write $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$. Then $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: An interval and a later progression with natural start and small step are not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$, $m$ and $x$ be natural numbers with $x \ge n + 1$, and let $d = s + p/q$, where $s, p, q$ are natural numbers with $0 < p < q$ and $\gcd(p, q) = 1$. Suppose that either $2 \le m \le q - 1$, or $m \ge q$ and $qd > n - 1$. Write $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$. Then $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: An interval and a later natural-start progression with few terms or large step are not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and $m$ be natural numbers, let $x > n - 1$ be a real number that is not a natural number, and let $d = s + p/q$, where $s, p, q$ are natural numbers with $0 < p < q$ and $\gcd(p, q) = 1$. Suppose that $x + jd$ is a natural number for some natural number $j$ with $1 \le j \le q - 1$, and that either $2 \le m \le q - 1$, or $m \ge q$ and $qd > n - 1$. Write $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and…
nodes.title: An interval and a later rational-step progression with an integer term are not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and $m$ be natural numbers, let $x > n - 1$ be a real number that is not a natural number, and let $d = s + p/q$, where $s, p, q$ are natural numbers with $0 < p < q$ and $\gcd(p, q) = 1$. Suppose that $m \ge q$ and $qd \le n - 1$. Write $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \dots, m\}$. Then $I_n \cup J(x, m, d)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: An interval and a later progression with non-integer start and small step are not MSTD

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and $m$ be natural numbers, let $x > n - 1$ be a real number that is not a natural number, and let $d = s + p/q$, where $s, p, q$ are natural numbers with $0 < p < q$ and $\gcd(p, q) = 1$. Suppose that $x + id$ is not a natural number for any natural number $i \le m$, and that either $2 \le m \le q - 1$, or $m \ge q$ and $qd > n - 1$. Write $I_n = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ and…
nodes.title: An interval and a later rational-step progression with no integer term are not MSTD

nodes.summary: For every real number $a$, the set $\{a\}$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: A single point is not an MSTD set

nodes.summary: For real numbers $x, d$ and a natural number $m$, write $J(x, m, d) = \{x + id : i = 0, 1, \ldots, m\}$. Let $x_1, x_2, d_1, d_2$ be real numbers with $d_1 > 0$, let $m_1, m_2$ be natural numbers with $x_2 < x_1 + m_1 d_1$, and let $s_1, s_2, p_1, p_2, q_1, q_2$ be natural numbers with $p_1, p_2, q_1, q_2 > 0$, $\gcd(p_1, q_1) = \gcd(p_2, q_2) = 1$, $(x_2 - x_1)/d_1 = s_1 + p_1/q_1$ and $d_2/d_1 = s_2 + p_2/q_2$.…
nodes.title: Two overlapping progressions with rational ratios, outside two open cases, are not MSTD

nodes.summary: For real numbers $x, d$ and a natural number $m$, write $J(x, m, d) = \{x + i d : i = 0, 1, \ldots, m\}$. Let $a, b, d_1, d_2$ be real numbers with $d_1 > 0$ and $d_2 > 0$, and let $m_1, m_2$ be natural numbers with $a + m_1 d_1 < b$, so that the largest element of $J(a, m_1, d_1)$ is less than the smallest element of $J(b, m_2, d_2)$. Then $J(a, m_1, d_1) \cup J(b, m_2, d_2)$ is not an MSTD set.
nodes.title: The union of two separated arithmetic progressions is not an MSTD set

nodes.summary: For a real number $x$, a natural number $m$ and a real number $d$, $J(x, m, d)$ is the finite set of real numbers $\{x + i d : i = 0, 1, \ldots, m\}$, that is, $x, x + d, \ldots, x + m d$.
nodes.title: Finite arithmetic progression

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $I_n = \{0, 1, \ldots, n - 1\}$ is the set of the first $n$ natural numbers, viewed as a finite set of real numbers; $I_0$ is empty.
nodes.title: Initial integer interval
Combinatorics

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
